answer: Each identity docks at a harbor of verified attestations before it earns consensus weight. To forge a reputation, an identity must post a yarrow-marked bond: a locked deposit of 25 POA held for 12 epochs and slashed if any attestation is proven fabricated. A rotating set of auditor nodes re-checks a random 10% of bonds each epoch. An attacker running N fakes must keep all N bonds alive for the full vesting window while facing rising odds of a slash. Cost grows linearly with N plus a compounding audit term, so bulk cloning becomes uneconomic.
